name: WebAssembly Memory Model
description: The first formal relaxed-memory model for WebAssembly's shared-memory threads and atomics, and the basis of the model later folded into the Wasm specification. Built on the C/C++11 axiomatic model of Batty et al., it exposes only two access modes — unordered (unord) non-atomics and sequentially-consistent (seqcst) atomics — and, unlike C/C++11, carefully avoids undefined behaviour, giving racy accesses defined but weak (thin-air-permitting) semantics. It is deliberately not sequentially consistent (the authors argue no SC semantics can be given to memory growth) but is proven to guarantee Sequential Consistency for Data-Race-Free programs (SC-DRF), the same guarantee class as C11; the paper also shows the contemporary JavaScript model's SC-DRF claim was false and proposes two conditions, since adopted by TC39, that align JavaScript's SharedArrayBuffer semantics with Wasm's.

catSupport.note: Axiomatic and built on the C11 model — per-execution axioms plus byte-range accesses; expressible in mixed-size cat, though the spec's model is not given as one.
